properties.arch_context_note: Located in the North Pennine & Northumberland sandstone/whin upland, this 4253 m² topographic anomaly (+2.72 m local relief, 0.148 / 8.4° mean scarp slope, nDSM 0.37 m) mimics prehistoric earthwork geometry in 1 m LiDAR but is automatically separated by the spatial/geometric filter as 'highway=track'. Steep machine-graded scarps, negative-relief extraction pits, or mapped modern infrastructure distinguish it from weathered prehistoric mounds despite proximity to Incised rocks on Gled Law (NHLE #1006558, 160 m S) and Two camps and cup and ring marked rocks on Dod Law (NHLE #1002946, 340 m NW).
